summary: @servicetitan/launchdarkly-service 38.1.2 preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory and immediately invokes it on the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync (falling back to a system `bun` on PATH if present). math_init.js is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle with string-array shuffling (function `WV8StW` rotating a >1000-entry mixed numeric/string array) and hex-scrambled identifiers; its behavior cannot be inspected without executing it under Bun. Neither the Bun runtime nor math_init.js has any relationship to the package's advertised LaunchDarkly-wrapper purpose. package.json also declares `"files": ["dist", "src"]` and `"sideEffects": false`, yet setup.mjs and math_init.js ship at the tarball root and are wired into a preinstall hook — a mismatch between the declared manifest and shipped contents consistent with payload smuggling into a legitimate-looking @servicetitan-scoped release. The alternate-runtime execution chain (download second runtime, then execute an obfuscated bundled blob under it) evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolvable code, and fires automatically on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
